recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-5273 unless OO chooses a broader editorial refresh of Observation examples independent of this 2015 ballot disposition.
issue_request: FHIR-5273 was a Published OO ballot change resolved Persuasive with Modification. It requested clearer Observation scope examples for laboratory data, imaging results such as bone density or fetal measurements, and device measurements such as EKG/pulse oximetry data, plus boundary text saying laboratory, pathology, and imaging reports belong in DiagnosticReport while Observation provides atomic results.
initial_application: Commit e6fbaaa95201041fcc6a3680731e9defca16311e (#5273, #5274) applied the Observation introduction changes in 2015 by adding the imaging-results bullet, revising device-measurement examples, and adding the DiagnosticReport boundary paragraph. Commit 1a1a9868d5186613a0e3aa02a2676638d36968f8 later added parallel DiagnosticReport boundary wording.
additional_context: Observation and DiagnosticReport are active resources in source/fhir.ini; the DSTU1 DeviceObservationReport artifact is now under removed-resources. Later Jira FHIR-11188 reinforced the current DiagnosticReport-context sentence, and FHIR-29032 broadened Observation to product/substance testing while preserving the lab/imaging/diagnostic-report relationship. A 2025 cleanup removed the old linked pulse-oximetry example from the device-measurements bullet after the example file was removed, but oxygen saturation remains covered in the vital-signs profile and the omission does not change FHIR-5273's semantic guidance.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current source/observation/observation-introduction.xml includes DiagnosticReport context, the imaging-results example, the device-measurement example, and the boundary paragraph; source/diagnosticreport/diagnosticreport-introduction.xml contains matching report boundary text. Restoring only a removed example link or duplicating existing prose would not improve the current specification.
